subject: another logistic regression with Design question

messages.author: ba6aaf9eec6afe60
messages.subject: another logistic regression with Design question
parts:
I have a question about the intercept in lrm in the Design package:

In chapter 5, section 4 of Stephan's Statistics for Linguists with R,
model.lrm is used with a binary dependent variable (CONSTRUCTION1), a
binary independent variable (V_CHANGPOSS), and two scaled independent
variables (REC_ACT and PAT_ACT). In the results, the Intercept
represents the default level of the V_CHANGPOSS factor
(V_CHANGPOSS=change) and the next line lists the other level of the
same factor, V_CHANGPOSS=no_change.

So far, so good - my question is how to interpret the results when
there is more than one categorical independent variable, or when the
categorical independent variables have more than two levels.

For example: a model with a binary dependent variable (Voice) with two
levels (Passive, Active), and three independent variables. One
variable (Len) is scalar; the other two are categorical: Ani, 4 levels
and Def, with 6 levels.

This produces the following output:
Intercept -1.51968 0.32333 -4.7 0
Ani=b -0.51932 0.30098 -1.73 0.0845
Ani=b -0.4329 0.29655 -1.46 0.1444
Ani=b -1.29995 0.34235 -3.8 0.0001
Def=b -0.20174 0.13611 -1.48 0.1383
Def=c 0.12944 0.12299 1.05 0.2926
Def=d -0.06962 1.06212 -0.07 0.9477
Def=e -0.93456 0.52972 -1.76 0.0777
Def=f -0.40812 0.18146 -2.25 0.0245
Len -0.0393 0.02588 -1.52 0.1288

It looks like the Intercept is a combination of the first level of Ani
and the first level of Def. Is there a way to do this analysis without
an intercept?

Thanks for you help!
~Linnea

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] another logistic regression with Design  question
parts:
This can best be answered with code:

# set up
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))
library(Design)
logit<-function(x) { log(x/(1-x)) }
ilogit<-function(x) { 1/(1+exp(-x)) }

# generate random data
set.seed(3)
x1 <- factor(sample(letters[1:3], 500, replace=TRUE))
x2 <- factor(sample(letters[4:6], 500, replace=TRUE))
x3 <- factor(sample(letters[8:10], 500, replace=TRUE))
y <-factor(sample(letters[25:26], 500, replace=TRUE))

# fit a model
m1 <- lrm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3)

# inspect predictions
ilogit(coef(m1)) # inverse logit of the intercept =
tapply(predict(m1, type="fitted.ind"), list(x1, x2, x3), mean)[1,1,1]
# the predicted probability when all independent vars are at their
first level


Cheers,
STG
